etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from Middle French piquant (“pricking, stimulating, irritating”), present participle of piquer, possibly from Old French pikier (“to prick, sting, nettle”). Doublet of picong. Related to pike.
senses: (archaic) Causing hurt feelings; scathing, severe. [from 16th c.]
Stimulating to the senses; engaging; charming. [from 17th c.]
